bounded_correction_the_packet_needs: sections 5 and 6 swap for a fresh installation: install -> START -> create -> observe.
cause: job_manager._create opens the control store with ControlStore.open_readonly. The only supported writable open is job_manager._serve (ControlStore.open), which is what tools/stack.py:start launches with --control. So the control store is created by STARTING the deployment.
command: manager --store <jobs> --incarnation operator-1 --authority-uuid <minted> create --instance <dest> --control <control> --authority <authority> ... (the packet's section 5, verbatim)
corroboration: the installer's own closing message tells the operator to start next, and the emitted capacity note says a fresh instance 'serves a real idle scheduler and publisher over empty stores' -- starting before any Job is the designed path

db_at_the_time.jobs.sqlite3: present (create made it before the control open)

how_this_execution_proceeds: by starting first, which is the supported order. That reorders two already-authorized operations; it adds no operation, repairs no unrelated state, and re-admits no Job (none had been admitted).
refusal: baton_v12.contracts.errors.ContractRefusal: a read-only manager requires an existing regular store
what: the accepted packet publishes `create` (section 5) BEFORE `start` (section 6). On a fresh installation that order cannot work: `create` opens the control store READ-ONLY and the control store does not exist until the serve loop creates it.
why_my_own_proof_did_not_catch_it: prove_capacity.py:_create opened the control store itself with ControlStore.open before calling create. That harness step was never published in the packet, so the packet's order was never exercised as published.
